value.overview: The Short-tailed Hawk is a small to medium-sized bird of prey found from the southern United States through Central America and much of South America. It is named for its relatively short tail, although its broad wings are often the most noticeable feature in flight. Two main color forms occur: a pale form with a mostly white underside and a dark form that appears nearly black below. It often hunts by soaring over forest edges and open areas.
value.classification: The Short-tailed Hawk belongs to the hawk and eagle family Accipitridae and the genus Buteo. Its scientific name is Buteo brachyurus.
value.identification: Adults have broad wings, a short tail, and yellow legs and cere. In the pale form, the upperparts are dark brown while the underparts are largely white, with dark flight feathers and a dark trailing edge to the wings. The dark form is deep brown to black below but usually shows pale areas at the bases of the flight feathers when viewed from beneath. Immatures are generally browner and more heavily streaked, especially on the breast. The species may soar with wings held slightly raised.
value.rangeHabitat: The Short-tailed Hawk ranges from southern Florida and northern Mexico south through Central America to northern Argentina. In Costa Rica it is an uncommon, local resident, reported especially along lower mountain slopes and ridges on the Caribbean side of the Central and Tilarán ranges, around the Arenal lowlands, and on both slopes of the Guanacaste range. It also occurs in forest, scattered-tree landscapes, forest patches, savannas, and open country near woodland. Records are more frequent in the Caribbean lowlands than in many Pacific lowland areas.
value.migrationStatus: Costa Rica supports resident birds as well as seasonal migrants. Migration is especially noticeable from August to October and from February to April, when individuals may appear in or near larger movements of other hawks. Birds from northern populations can move south into Costa Rica, while many birds farther south are resident.
value.breeding: The species generally nests in tall trees within or beside mature, often wet forest, including forest near wetlands or water. It usually lays a small clutch, and both adults participate in territorial defense and care of the young. The nest is a stick platform placed high above the ground. In Costa Rica, the species is considered resident in some mountainous regions, but reliable published information on its nesting distribution and breeding biology within the country is limited.
value.dietFeeding: Short-tailed Hawks mainly take small birds, which they often catch during fast, agile attacks from above or while maneuvering near forest edges. They also eat reptiles, amphibians, insects, and occasionally small mammals. The hawk commonly hunts from a soaring position, using rising air over open ground or forest margins to search for prey. Its relatively broad wings support both soaring and sudden changes in direction during pursuit.
value.behavior: This hawk is usually solitary outside the breeding season, although several may be seen during migration or in areas with favorable soaring conditions. It spends much of the day perched quietly or circling high above ridges, clearings, and forest edges. Migrating birds may travel in a relatively direct, sustained flight rather than continuously soaring. The species is generally unobtrusive and can be difficult to detect unless it is flying overhead.
